title: Plurinodal alteration over an excellent trait and smooth alteration over a field
statement:
Let $B$ be an excellent strictly henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] trait of equal characteristic $p>0$, with algebraically closed residue field, generic point $\eta$, and chosen geometric generic point $\bar\eta$; a trait means the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring. Let $X\to B$ be integral, proper, of finite type, and dominant [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. There is a finite extension of traits $B'\to B$, with a compatible choice of $\bar\eta$, such that every irreducible component of $(X\times_BB')_{\mathrm{red}}$ dominating $B'$ admits a proper, dominant, generically finite map $P\to (X\times_BB')_{\mathrm{red}}$ onto that component, where $P\to B'$ is a tower of projective flat curves with geometrically connected fibres and at worst ordinary double points. Each such curve has an open smooth locus whose closed complement is finite over its base. A tower of length zero is $B'$ itself. An ordinary double point means a point whose completed geometric local ring in the fibre is $\Omega[[x,y]]/(xy)$.

For an integral proper finite-type scheme $X$ over an algebraically closed field $F$ of characteristic $p>0$, there is a smooth proper $F$-scheme $P$ and a proper dominant generically finite map $P\to X$. Here generically finite means finite over some dense open of $X$; no invertibility of its degree is required.

Excellence of a scheme means excellence of its affine coordinate rings [def-exc-excellent-ring].
